note: Magasin should lead with the everyday shop/store sense. 'Barn' is not an appropriate core modern learner gloss; storage/warehouse/magazine senses are secondary.
Quartier normally means neighborhood/district/quarter. The current wording incorrectly narrows neighborhood to an impoverished suburban area.
Intéressant is an adjective and also the present participle of intéresser, which the gloss explicitly mentions but the POS omits.
proposed_english: interesting; interesting/engaging; present participle of intéresser

note: Demande is both the noun request/demand and a common finite/imperative form of demander. The current entry mentions only the imperative while POS remains noun-only.
proposed_english: request; demand; asks/requests; ask/request! (forms of demander, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Laisse is the noun leash/lead but is also an extremely common finite and imperative form of laisser, as in laisse-moi. The current rare foreshore sense should not hide this.
proposed_english: leash; lead; leaves/lets; leave!/let! (forms of laisser, context-dependent); foreshore (specialized)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Ennui means boredom but also trouble/problem/annoyance, especially in plural or fixed expressions. The current gloss is too narrow.
La is the feminine article/object pronoun, and noun POS is listed because la is also the musical note A. That noun meaning is missing.
proposed_english: the (feminine singular); her; it; A/la (musical note)

note: Enceinte means pregnant as an adjective and, as nouns, a speaker or an enclosure/compound. 'Interior' is an imprecise noun gloss.
Débarrasser is normally learned as clear/remove and especially se débarrasser de = get rid of. Bare 'rid' is not usable learner English.
proposed_english: to clear; to remove; to rid; to get rid of (se débarrasser de)

note: Adresse centrally means address. The current entry omits that basic meaning and leads with secondary senses such as skill/adroitness.
Morceau should teach piece/bit/slice and piece of music. 'Gun, piece' is an obsolete/specialized sense and should not lead a learner entry.
proposed_english: piece; bit; slice; morsel; piece of music/work

note: Causer centrally means cause and, informally, talk/chat. 'Speak a language' is not a suitable core learner definition.
proposed_english: to cause; to talk; to chat (informal)

note: Oser means dare/venture. 'To be allowed to' is not a direct core meaning and can misteach the verb.
proposed_english: to dare; to venture; to have the nerve/courage to
